articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft delivers a whopping 167 vulnerabilities in April's Patch Tuesday, including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. When your monthly security update looks like a phone book, maybe it's time to question some life choices.

articles.title: Trellix Confirms Source Code Breach With Unauthorized Repository Access
articles.summary: CISA adds CVE-2026-31431 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as attackers are actively rooting Linux boxes in the wild. Another day, another privilege escalation turning users into gods of their own digital domains.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability already being exploited with ransomware demands hitting victims before patches even landed. Millions of sites potentially exposed because apparently we're still learning that 'patch first, ask questions later' isn't optional.

articles.title: 30,000 Facebook Accounts Hacked via Google AppSheet Phishing Campaign
articles.summary: Cybersecurity company Trellix gets breached with unauthorized source code access, proving that even the defenders aren't immune to getting pwned. The irony is so thick you could cut it with a compromised certificate.

articles.title: CVE-2026-31431: Copy Fail vulnerability enables Linux root privilege escalation across cloud environments
articles.summary: France opens probe into 15-year-old who allegedly hacked the national ID agency and tried selling millions of citizens' data on the dark web. Kid's got entrepreneurial spirit, just needs better career guidance.

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: Public records laws expose ALPR surveillance abuses, so naturally states want to block transparency efforts. Because nothing says 'we're the good guys' like frantically covering up mass surveillance programs when citizens start asking questions.

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's new anti-VPN law goes into effect, because apparently privacy tools are now the enemy of freedom. Watch VPN usage spike as residents realize their state government thinks anonymity is a bug, not a feature.

articles.title: Brace for the patch tsunami: AI is unearthing decades of buried code debt
articles.summary: FBI redirects 9,000 personnel to immigration enforcement under Trump's deportation push, potentially compromising national security. Nothing says 'protecting America' like gutting your cybercrime units to chase paperwork violations.

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Britain's cyber agency warns that AI is about to unleash decades of buried code vulnerabilities all at once. The technical debt chickens are coming home to roost, and they're bringing their entire extended family.

articles.title: ADT data breach exposes customer information
articles.summary: CopyFail Linux vulnerability allows any user to escalate to root privileges across most distributions and kernels. Local privilege escalation strikes again, proving that sometimes the call is coming from inside the house.
